Approach and Rationale
The core objective is to minimize the evaluation function: 2 * n * max(conv) / sum(a)^2, where conv is the full convolution of the sequence. This differs from the previous program that used a strategy of testing multiple lengths and interpolation. To achieve a better result, I will commit to a fixed length of 1024 (doubled from their initial length) with the strong hypothesis that longer sequences inherently reduce this parameter space. The reason is that the uniform sequence projected to 1024 may yield a significantly lower objective value than their 512-length results, even if the convolution peak becomes slightly higher. The optimization leverages the observation that increasing resolution allows the gradient descent to explore smaller step sizes and get closer to the theoretical minimum.

The previous program's mixed approach might have been computationally expensive (splitting time) and now risks falling into local optima. The proposed approach centers the search in the main optimization phase itself, treating the parent sequence not as a known entity but as a point of departure. Due to increased resolution (1024), standard deviation might be more effective as a momentum component.
